paper_title: Analyzing the Challenges and Solutions of Sustainable Groundwater Management using Micro-irrigation

paper_identity.paper_title: Analyzing the Challenges and Solutions of Sustainable Groundwater Management using Micro-irrigation

paper_summary: This narrative review synthesizes roughly fifty English-language studies on micro-irrigation, irrigation systems, and groundwater sustainability, with Indian policy context (PMKSY, NMMI, CSS) and national groundwater statistics. It argues micro-irrigation can conserve groundwater by cutting losses and raising water-use efficiency and yields, but poor design, excessive application, agrochemical pathways, and rebound under weak governance can worsen depletion and quality risks.
study_region: Global literature with explicit India policy, statistics, and case examples (e.g., Rajasthan, NMMI); authors affiliated Punjab, India
study_period: Literature search limited to publications roughly over the prior 15 years from manuscript date; national groundwater statistics cited as of 2022
methodology: Systematic-style literature search (SCI, Scopus, Web of Science), deduplication, title/abstract/full-text screening, qualitative synthesis of ~50 papers plus Indian government reports.
paper_type_rationale: The article compiles and narrates findings across many prior studies and reports rather than presenting new primary measurements or causal identification from a single dataset.

important_variables.significance: Dominant share of national water use (91% cited) and central to both depletion and MI efficiency narratives.
Core technology lever for WUE, recharge-friendly return flows, yield gains, and rebound risk depending on governance.
Primary mechanism through which MI is argued to reduce seasonal applied water in cited quantitative studies.
Outcome axis for sustainability: national overdraft story and regional Green Revolution legacy.
Anchors the water-balance framing (recharge vs extraction numbers cited from 2022 report).

important_variables_narrative: The review positions irrigation_demand—especially groundwater-based irrigation—as the main stressor on aquifers, using national extraction and drained-resource statistics alongside the Green Revolution legacy in northwest India. NEW_micro_irrigation_adoption and NEW_water_use_efficiency are treated as the primary levers to cut losses and align applications with crop needs, with meta-regression and trial magnitudes on seasonal water savings and yield responses. However, the same adoption variable interacts with governance: the Rajasthan example flags rebound-style intensification when regulations are weak, while salinity_level captures quality risks from return flows and agrochemical pathways. For district work, national aggregates here should be downscaled with CGWB/WRIS block indicators rather than applied literally.
